speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you haven't provided any symptoms or history yet. To begin our evaluation, have you experienced any confusion, memory loss, or changes in your personality recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old female. The patient has been brought to the emergency room by her family due to altered mental status. The family mentions that she has been increasingly confused over the past few days. No recent head trauma or known drug use. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack-years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given her smoking history and acute confusion, have you noticed any signs of respiratory distress, such as shortness of breath, or any recent changes in her lung function?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mental status changes. I also have Increased confusion, Lethargy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.

The combination of acute confusion, lethargy, and a significant smoking history (30 pack-years) strongly suggests inhalation of toxic gases. Please confirm if the patient has been exposed to smoke or fumes in a closed environment recently. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Head (to rule out structural causes).
